verdict.summary: OpenWeather does not use OAuth, so there is no OAuth app to register. Access uses an account API key (the appid parameter), issued with no approval step. The only waits are email confirmation and key activation, which can take up to 2 hours. For scale, the limits are your plan's call caps and billing, not a review.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Minutes to about 2 hours (key activation delay)

gates.name: Account API key (free access)
gates.unlocks: Your own key works on free Weather API endpoints (current weather, 5-day forecast, air pollution, maps, geocoding) once it is activated.
limits: Keys activate automatically up to 2 hours after registration. An invalid-key error before then is expected.
Limits apply to the whole account, summed across all keys and products
gates.time_to_reach: About 10 minutes of setup, plus up to 2 hours for the key to activate

gates.name: No separate test tier (same key, shared account limits)
gates.unlocks: There is no test-user allowlist or dev mode. The key you already have can serve any users of your agent, within your account's call limits.
limits: No per-user or install cap is documented
All usage counts toward your account-level limit
If you go over a limit you get an email asking you to upgrade. The key is suspended only if you don't reply.

gates.name: Production use (paid plan if needed)
gates.unlocks: Public use at higher volume through self-service paid plans (Startup to Expert, up to 100,000 calls/minute), One Call API 4.0 pay-per-call, or an enterprise agreement.
limits: No app review, domain verification or security assessment is documented
One Call subscriptions need a credit card. The first 1,000 calls per day are free on One Call 4.0.
You must credit OpenWeather when you display its data (ODbL licence)
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes (self-service checkout). Enterprise terms go through sales.

steps.title: Confirm that OAuth doesn't apply here
steps.detail: OpenWeather offers no OAuth authorize endpoint, and Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit or managed OAuth app. Plan to use an API key sent as the appid query parameter instead of an OAuth client ID and secret.
gotchas: There is no redirect URI, no scopes and no client secret to configure.

steps.title: Create an OpenWeather account and accept the terms
steps.detail: Sign up at openweathermap.org and accept the terms of sale, website terms and privacy policy. Read them before you subscribe to any paid service.

steps.title: Confirm your email address
steps.detail: Click the confirmation link in the signup email. Your API key then appears on the account's API keys page, and the welcome email also contains it.

steps.title: Generate a dedicated key for your agent
steps.detail: Sign in and open the API keys page. Generate an extra key with a name that identifies your agent, so you can delete or rotate it without affecting other uses. You can delete any key as long as at least one remains.
gotchas: Extra keys don't add capacity: every key on the account shares one call limit.

steps.title: Wait for the key to activate
steps.detail: New keys activate automatically up to 2 hours after registration. An invalid-key error during this window is normal.

steps.title: Run a test call with the key
steps.detail: Call a free endpoint such as current weather with the key in the appid query parameter, and check that you get data back instead of an invalid-key error. OpenWeather processes only requests that carry a key.

steps.title: Store the key in Composio or your agent
steps.detail: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit, so set the key up as an API-key credential, either in a custom Composio integration (if your setup supports one) or directly in your agent's secrets. Never put it in an OAuth flow.
gotchas: Whether Composio can broker a custom API-key connection for OpenWeather has not been confirmed.

steps.title: Add caching and rate limiting
steps.detail: Request each location no more than once every 10 minutes, and cache results so you stay under the per-minute and monthly limits. Daily limits reset between 00:00 and 00:05 UTC.

steps.title: Show OpenWeather attribution
steps.detail: Add credit to OpenWeather wherever your agent displays its data, as the ODbL licence requires. If you store results and offer them as a dataset outside your organisation, share-alike conditions may apply.

steps.title: Pick a paid plan or One Call subscription if needed
steps.detail: If the free allowance isn't enough, or you need One Call API 4.0, subscribe on the pricing page. One Call needs a credit card on file. For contract terms or very high volume, contact OpenWeather enterprise sales.

steps.title: Watch for usage-limit emails
steps.detail: Reply to any over-limit email from OpenWeather. If you don't, your key can be suspended, and HTTP 429 errors mean you've hit a daily or monthly limit.

requirements.detail: You must confirm your email before the key appears on the API keys page.
Terms of sale, website terms and privacy policy.
Free tier: 60 calls/minute and 1,000,000 calls/month, summed across all keys and products on the account.
Required wherever your app displays data under the ODbL licence.

requirements.item: Credit card for One Call subscriptions
requirements.detail: One Call needs a card on file. The free access APIs don't.

scopes.effect: There are no scopes. The key is the only credential, and which products you can use depends on your subscription and the endpoint you call.

blockers.symptom: Invalid API key error right after signup
blockers.cause: The key hasn't activated yet. Activation can take up to 2 hours.
blockers.fix: Wait up to 2 hours and try again.

blockers.cause: Your account went over its daily or monthly call limit.
blockers.fix: Reduce calls (cache each location for 10 minutes) or upgrade your plan. A daily block clears at the next reset (00:00-00:05 UTC), even if you raise the limit.

blockers.symptom: Key suspended after an over-limit email
blockers.cause: Nobody replied to OpenWeather's over-limit notice.
blockers.fix: Reply to the notice and upgrade to a paid plan or reduce usage.

blockers.symptom: Usage hits the limit sooner than expected
blockers.cause: Limits are shared across every key and product on the account.
blockers.fix: Use a separate account for the agent, or size your plan to cover combined usage.

blockers.symptom: No OAuth authorize endpoint or Composio toolkit
blockers.fix: Use the appid key as an API-key credential.

blockers.symptom: Need help using the key inside your own app
blockers.cause: OpenWeather doesn't provide technical support for third-party apps that use its keys.
blockers.fix: Rely on the public docs. Your app is your responsibility.

composio.note: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit and no managed OAuth app, and OpenWeather doesn't offer OAuth at all, so there is nothing to choose between managed and own-app auth. Use your own account API key (appid) as an API-key credential. Whether Composio supports a custom API-key connection for this provider has not been checked.

evidence.claim: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit, so there is no managed OAuth app, no default scopes and no authorize/token URLs.
The conventional OAuth authorize path on the OpenWeather account host returns a 404 page, not an OAuth error.
evidence.quote: The page you were looking for doesn't exist (404)

Every call must include the key as the appid parameter.
A key is issued instantly with no approval or onboarding step.

open_questions: OpenWeather hasn't explicitly said it offers no OAuth. That conclusion rests on a 404 probe and the absence of any OAuth docs.
Can Composio broker a custom API-key connection for OpenWeather?
Do the terms of sale or website terms prohibit embedding API keys in shipped client apps? (The PDFs were not fetched.)
Does OpenWeather have a partner program with its own review process?
Are there per-key limits beyond the account-level free-tier figures?
